families.title: Authorization, approval, scope and lifecycle
review_questions: Are all executable decisions and lifecycle transitions loaded from trusted current source of truth?
Do omitted, stale or caller-controlled scope, target, approval, adapter or lifecycle fields fail closed?
Were all public entry points, alternate callers and sibling state transitions audited?

families.title: Secrets, plaintext and LLM-visible data
review_questions: Can secret values or raw output reach prompts, normal storage, logs, exceptions or reports?
Do every public resolve, read, export and recovery path enforce the same reference-only boundary?

families.title: Integrity, authenticated encryption and key domains
review_questions: Are digests, IDs, bindings, algorithms, nonces and key domains checked on both write and read?
Do rotation, revocation and unavailable-key paths fail closed without plaintext or cross-domain fallback?

families.title: Audit, retry, recovery and durable state
review_questions: Are crash, retry, reconciliation and unknown-outcome transitions complete and non-duplicating?
Are audit ordering, integrity and recovery decisions derived from durable trusted state?

families.title: Filesystem, concurrency, quota and retention
review_questions: Are traversal, symlink, race, atomicity, ownership, quota and cleanup paths covered?
Are retention and lease decisions based on trusted time and durable current state?

families.title: Untrusted parsing, schemas and output boundaries
review_questions: Are duplicate keys, unknown fields, coercion, malformed metadata and prompt injection rejected at the actual boundary?
Do alternate parsers and compatibility readers preserve the same fail-closed behavior?

families.title: Acceptance completeness and earlier-phase compatibility
review_questions: Does every acceptance criterion have positive, negative and failure-path evidence?
Do changed interfaces preserve every earlier-phase invariant and supported caller?
